analysis.investment_thesis: Devyani is a QSR franchisee — it operates other people's brands (KFC, Pizza Hut, Costa Coffee) at high debt and has been unable to generate positive net profit in 7 of its last 9 reported years. A forward P/E of 127x on a loss-making business with D/E of 1.71 and rising finance costs of INR 267 Cr is unjustifiable under any valuation framework I use.
key_strengths: Operating cash flow positive all 5 years (INR 900 Cr in FY25) and free cash flow growing, showing the store-level economics work
Revenue CAGR of 19.3% over 9 years confirms genuine consumer demand for its brands in India
High promoter holding (61.37%) signals ownership commitment
key_risks: D/E of 1.71 with borrowings jumping from INR 1,254 Cr (FY22) to INR 3,343 Cr (FY25) — debt is growing faster than the business
Finance costs of INR 267 Cr in FY25 overwhelm operating profit of INR 839 Cr, leaving virtually nothing for shareholders
Company does not own the brands it operates — KFC and Pizza Hut licences can be repriced or terminated by Yum! Brands
red_flags: Net profit was negative in 7 of 9 years — chronic unprofitability at the bottom line is a fundamental flaw, not a temporary setback
Forward P/E of 127.2x on a business that lost money in FY24 and FY25 is pure speculation on a distant and uncertain recovery
Borrowings nearly tripled from FY22 to FY25 (INR 1,254 Cr to INR 3,343 Cr) — debt-funded expansion without earnings to service it
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The QSR franchise model is capital-intensive: Devyani must fit out restaurants, pay royalties to brand owners, and manage perishable supply chains — all while having zero pricing power on the brand itself. EBITDA looks healthy at INR 853 Cr, but EBITDA obscures the real economic reality once you subtract lease costs, interest, and depreciation from the actual P&L.

I want businesses that earn high returns on tangible equity, own their competitive advantage, and generate cash for shareholders. Devyani owns none of its brands, earns 0.54% ROE, and is leveraged 1.71x. At 127x forward earnings, the market is pricing perfection into a business that has delivered chronic losses. That is precisely the kind of setup where permanent capital loss becomes a real risk.
